items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to transportation network companies
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4108

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to transportation
network companies

PURPOSE:

To clarify insurance provisions and requirements relative to
transportation network companies.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of this bill would add a new section 3441 to the insurance
law dealing with transportation network companies. The bill defines
"transportation network companies" and sets forth the auto insurance
coverage which is required to cover transportation network company
activities. The bill also clarifies that, unless otherwise expressly
provided for, the vehicle owner's personal auto insurance policy shall
not provide coverage for transportation network company activities
from the moment a participating driver logs on to the transportation
network company's online-enabled application or platform until the
driver logs off the online-enabled application or platform or the
passenger exits the vehicle, whichever is later. The bill also
requires transportation network companies or their insurers to
cooperate with insurers that are involved in any claims coverage
investigation to facilitate the exchange of relevant information,
including dates and times of any accidents involving participating
drivers and the times the driver logged on and off the transportation
network company's online-enabled application or platform.

Section two of this bill sets forth the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

Services offered by transportation network companies (TNC) are a
relatively new trend in major cities across the country.
Transportation network companies (also refereed to as "ride-share"
companies) use smartphone communications technology to connect
individuals who want a ride with drivers for a fee. Because the
drivers generally use their personal vehicles, there are insurance
coverage issues, as the typical standard personal automobile insurance
policy contains a "livery" exclusion which applies when the vehicle is
being rented out, or used to carry passengers for hire.  Consequently,
most personal automobile insurance policies do not cover any damages
or losses when a car is being used for commercial ride-sharing. The
National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) and more than
20 state insurance departments and public service commissions have
issued consumer alerts or advisories highlighting the potential
insurance gaps in coverage for TNC activity and encouraging TNC
drivers to talk with their insurer to understand their exposure.

Legislation is necessary to eliminate these insurance gaps and ensure
that private passenger auto insurance policyholders are not forced to
subsidize TNC business activities. The California Public Utilities
Commission was the first regulatory body to regulate these activities


and in 2014, enacted AB 2293 which creates a firewall protecting
personal auto insurance from subsidizing commercial TNC activities and
ensures that adequate insurance coverage is required to be provided
for TNC activities from the time when the driver logs on to the TNC
application through the time when the driver logs off of the
application.

This bill would establish requirements and protections similar to
those which have been adopted in other states relative to TNCs so as
to ensure adequate coverage for TNC activities and prevent the
subsidization of commercial TNC activities by personal auto insurance
policyholders In New York, TNCs are currently operating only in New
York City pursuant to Taxi and Limousine Commission regulations This
bill would address the TNC insurance issues which are hindering TNCs
from operating upstate and would help to allow this innovative new
transportation option to be made available upstate To support
innovation and allow these new TNC businesses to grow while at the
same time protecting consumers, it is vitally important that the
vehicles used in TNC services are properly insured and the public is
protected. This bill would establish clear guidelines relative to TNC
related insurance issues so that everyone knows where they stand
regarding insurance coverage for transportation network services

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4108A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to
transportation network companies

PURPOSE: To clarify insurance provisions and requirements relative to
transportation network companies

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of this bill would add a new section 3441 to the insurance
law dealing with transportation network companies. The bill defines
"transportation network companies" and sets forth the auto insurance
coverage which is required to cover transportation network company
activities. The bill also clarifies that, unless otherwise expressly
provided for, the vehicle owner's personal auto insurance policy shall
not provide coverage for transportation network company activities
from the moment a participating driver logs on to the transportation
network company's online-enabled application or platform until the
driver logs off the online-enabled application or platform or' the
passenger exits the vehicle, whichever is later The bill also requires
transportation network companies or their insurers to cooperate with
insurers that are involved in any claims coverage investigation to
facilitate the exchange of relevant information, including dates and
times of any accidents involving participating drivers and the times
the driver logged on and off the transportation network company's
online-enabled application or platform.

Section two of this bill would add a new section 3445 to the insurance
law dealing with group insurance policies for transportation network
companies.

Section three of this bill amends subsection (b) of section 5103 of
the insurance law by adding a new paragraph 4 Section four of this
bill sets forth the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:  Services offered by transportation network companies
(TNC) are a relatively new trend in major cities across the country.
Transportation network companies (also referred to as "ride-share"
companies) use smartphone communications technology to connect
individuals who want a ride with drivers for a fee. Because the
drivers generally use their personal vehicles, there are insurance
coverage issues, as the typical standard personal automobile insurance
policy contains a "livery" exclusion which applies when the vehicle is
being rented out, or used to carry passenger's for hire.
Consequently, most personal automobile insurance policies do not cover
any damages or losses when a car is being used for commercial
ride-sharing. The National Association of Insurance Commissioners
(NAIC) and more than 20 state insurance departments and public service
commissions have issued consumer alerts or advisories highlighting the
potential insurance gaps in coverage for TNC activity and encouraging
TNC drivers to talk with their insurer to understand their exposure.

Legislation is necessary to eliminate these insurance gaps and ensure
that private passenger auto insurance policyholders are not forced to
subsidize TNC business activities. The California Public Utilities
Commission was the first regulatory body to regulate these activities


and in 2014, enacted AB 2293 which creates a firewall protecting
personal auto insurance from subsidizing commercial TNC activities and
ensures that adequate insurance coverage is required to be provided
for TNC activities from the time when the driver logs on to the TNC
application through the time when the driver logs off of the
application.

This bill would establish requirements and protections similar to
those which have been adopted in other states relative to TNCs so as
to ensure adequate coverage for TNC activities and prevent the
subsidization of commercial TNC activities by personal auto insurance
policyholders. In New York, TNCs are currently operating only in New
York City pursuant to Taxi and Limousine Commission regulations. This
bill would address the TNC insurance issues which are hindering TNCs
from operating upstate and would help to allow this innovative new
transportation option to be made available upstate. To support
innovation and allow these new TNC businesses to grow while at the
same time protecting consumers, it is vitally important that the
vehicles used in TNC services are properly insured and the public is
protected. This bill would establish clear guidelines relative to TNC
related insurance issues so that everyone knows where they stand
regarding insurance coverage for transportation network services.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None.

EFFECTIVE DATE: This act shall take effect on the one hundred
twentieth day after it shall have become law.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to transportation network companies
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4108B

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to transportation
network companies

PURPOSE:

To clarify insurance provisions and requirements relative to
transportation network companies.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections 1 and 2 of the bill amend the insurance law by adding two new
sections to authorize the issuance of automobile insurance policies to
transportation network companies and transportation network company
drivers on a group basis and to regulate the interaction of private
passenger automobile insurance policies with insurance policies
covering transportation network services.

Sections 3 amends the insurance law by adding as a permissible
exclusion from certain required coverages injuries that occur while
operating a personal vehicle as a transportation network company
driver.

Section 4 is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

Transportation Network Companies (TNCs) provide a digital platform
that matches consumers with a community of vetted local drivers
offering rides using their personal vehicles. Existing transportation
options alone can no longer fully accommodate growing populations, yet
80% of the seats in personal vehicles remain empty.  TNC platforms are
already filling those empty seats across the country by providing
additional transportation options to communities that need them most
and reducing the economic burden of car ownership.

The broader benefits of ridesharing are being realized in communities
where TNCs have been able to scale effectively. Ridesharing protects
consumer choice, responds to unmet market demands, supplies accessible
and affordable transportation options to underserved areas, provides
economic opportunities, reduces drunk driving, eases traffic
congestion, curbs air pollution and provides last mile solutions to
commuters seeking to utilize existing transit options.  TNCs are
continuing to evolve to maximize these benefits with innovative
options in the largest markets where they have been able to grow
within the framework of reasonable regulation.

This bill would establish requirements and protections similar to
those which have been adopted in other states relative to TNCs so as
to ensure adequate coverage for TNC activities and prevent the
subsidization of commercial TNC activities by personal auto insurance
policyholders. In New York, TNCs are currently operating only in New
York City pursuant to Taxi and Limousine Commission regulations. This
bill would address the TNC insurance issues which are hindering TNCs


from operating upstate and would help to allow this innovative new
transportation option to be made available upstate To support
innovation and allow these new TNC businesses to grow while at the
same time protecting consumers, it is vitally important that the
vehicles used in TNC services are properly insured and the public is
protected. This bill would establish clear guidelines relative to TNC
related insurance issues so that everyone knows where they stand
regarding insurance coverage for transportation network services. This
bill would balance the need to ensure that necessary safety standards
are met by existing and emerging TNCs while enabling growth and
innovation to fully realize the benefits that consumers are demanding.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately after it shall have become law.
